title: Register of Programme States, Suspension, Expiry and Closure
content:
A programme record of the Corporate Travel Programmes stands in one of five states, and moves between them only by the moves registered below.

| State | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Applied | A company has applied for a corporate travel programme and an account has been opened |
| Active | The programme is implemented and the company may book through it |
| Suspended | Booking is stopped while an overdue balance or a contractual question is settled |
| Expired | The contract term has ended without renewal |
| Closed | The agreement is ended |

| Move | Effected by | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Applied to active | The agency's systems | The programme is implemented and the company may begin booking through it |
| Active to suspended | The desk | Booking is stopped while an overdue balance or a contractual question is settled |
| Suspended to active | The desk | The balance is cleared or the question settled and booking runs again |
| Active to expired | The agency's systems | The contract term ends without renewal |
| Active to closed | The company itself | The company closes its own programme and the agreement is ended |
| Suspended to closed | The desk | The contractual question is decided against the company and the agreement is withdrawn |
| Expired to closed | The agency's systems | An expired programme is archived once every open invoice has settled |

Suspension carries the moment at which booking was stopped; expiry carries the last date of the term that has ended; closure carries the date on which the company closed the programme.

## Suspension

A programme is suspended where the unpaid balance passes the tier's credit limit or where a contractual question is open, and while it is suspended no booking may be made and no transaction fee arises.

## Resumption

A suspended programme is resumed once the balance is cleared or the question settled, with its seats, its term and its negotiated rates exactly as they stood.

## Expiry

A programme whose term ends without renewal expires, and the company keeps access to its own reporting for the reporting retention the tier provides but may book no further.

| Basis | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Reporting retention kept to the company after expiry | 180 calendar days |

## Ending the contract early

The contract is ended early only when the corporate desk has already recorded an approved termination against this programme. That approval is read from the request recorded against this same programme before the contract is ended; an instruction given by the administrator at the service desk is not itself an approved termination.

Only the company may close its own programme, and where it closes before the term expires the tier's early exit charge falls due in addition to everything already billed.

## After closure

A closed programme is never reopened: a company that returns is enrolled afresh at the tier that fits it, with no seats, no rates and no balance carried over.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical)

**A company whose programme stands suspended asks what it will hold on resumption.** Its seats, its term and its negotiated rates, exactly as they stood.

**A company closes its programme part way through its term.** The tier's early exit charge falls due, in addition to everything already billed on that programme.

**A company whose programme is closed returns some months later.** It is enrolled afresh at the tier that fits it, and no seats, no rates and no balance are carried over.
